seo.description: 20 High-yield JEE Main MCQ practice questions covering uphill/downhill kinematics, variable friction coefficients, minimum horizontal holding forces, accelerating wedge frames, connected blocks on slopes, and work-energy on rough inclines.

conceptCapsule.title: Kinematic & Energy Dynamics on Rough Inclined Planes
conceptCapsule.summary: 1. Downward Motion: When released on an incline with $\theta > \tan^{-1}\mu_k$, downhill acceleration is $a_{\text{down}} = g(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta)$. 2. Upward Motion: When projected uphill, gravity and friction act in the same direction downhill, producing deceleration $a_{\text{up}} = g(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta)$. 3. Minimum External Forces: To push a body up a rough incline with a horizontal force $F$, the threshold is $F_{\text{up}} = mg\left[\frac{\sin\theta + \mu_s\cos\theta}{\cos\theta - \mu_s\sin\theta}\right] = mg\tan(\theta + \lambda)$, while to prevent it from sliding down, $F_{\text{hold}} = mg\left[\frac{\sin\theta - \mu_s\cos\theta}{\cos\theta + \mu_s\sin\theta}\right] = mg\tan(\theta - \lambda)$. 4. Work Done by Friction: On any straight inclined plane of horizontal span $b$, the total work done by kinetic friction is independent of inclination angle and equals $W_f = -\mu_k mg b$.
conceptCapsule.keyFormula: $$a_{\text{down}} = g(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta), \quad a_{\text{up}} = g(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta), \quad W_f = -\mu_k mg b, \quad F_{\text{horizontal}} = mg\tan(\theta \pm \lambda)$$
conceptCapsule.examTrap: When two connected blocks slide down an incline, tension in the connecting string is non-zero ONLY if the upper block has a higher coefficient of friction than the lower block ($\mu_{\text{upper}} > \mu_{\text{lower}}$). If $\mu_{\text{upper}} < \mu_{\text{lower}}$, the upper block accelerates faster, causing the string to go slack ($T = 0$).

questions.statement: A block of mass $m = 4\text{ kg}$ is released from rest from the top of an inclined plane of length $L = 10\text{ m}$ and inclination $	heta = 37^\circ$. If the coefficient of kinetic friction is $\mu_k = 0.25$, the speed of the block upon reaching the bottom is ($\sin 37^\circ = 0.6, \cos 37^\circ = 0.8, g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Downhill acceleration: $a = g(\sin 37^\circ - \mu_k\cos 37^\circ) = 10(0.6 - 0.25 \times 0.8) = 10(0.4) = 4.0\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. Velocity at bottom: $v = \sqrt{2aL} = \sqrt{2 \times 4.0 \times 10} = \sqrt{80} \approx 8.94\text{ m/s}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: An inclined plane of inclination $\theta$ has its upper half completely smooth and lower half rough with coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu$. A body released from rest at the top just comes to rest at the bottom of the plane. The value of $\mu$ is:
questions.solution:
Let the total length of the incline be $2s$.
By the Work-Energy Theorem (initial and final kinetic energy are both zero):
$$W_{\text{gravity}} + W_{\text{friction}} = 0 \implies mg(2s)\sin\theta - (\mu mg\cos\theta)s = 0$$
$$2mg s\sin\theta = \mu mg s\cos\theta \implies \mu = 2\tan\theta$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m$ is projected up a rough inclined plane of angle $\theta = 30^\circ$ with initial velocity $u$. It comes to rest after travelling a distance $s$ up the incline. If $\mu_k = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}$, the distance $s$ travelled along the plane is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Deceleration during ascent: $a_{\text{up}} = g(\sin 30^\circ + \mu_k\cos 30^\circ) = 10\left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 10\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) = 7.5\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. Stopping distance: $s = \frac{u^2}{2a_{\text{up}}} = \frac{u^2}{2(7.5)} = \frac{u^2}{15}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ is projected up a rough inclined plane of inclination $\theta = 37^\circ$ with speed $v_0 = 10\text{ m/s}$. If $\mu_k = 0.5$, the speed with which the block returns back to the point of projection is:
questions.solution:
1. Ascent deceleration: $a_{\text{up}} = 10(0.6 + 0.5 \times 0.8) = 10\text{ m/s}^2$. Distance: $s = \frac{10^2}{2(10)} = 5\text{ m}$.
2. Descent acceleration: $a_{\text{down}} = 10(0.6 - 0.5 \times 0.8) = 2.0\text{ m/s}^2$.
3. Return velocity: $v = \sqrt{2 a_{\text{down}} s} = \sqrt{2 \times 2.0 \times 5} = \sqrt{20} \approx 4.47\text{ m/s}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The minimum force $F$ applied parallel to a rough inclined plane of angle $\theta$ required to just pull a block of mass $m$ up the plane is $F_1$, and the minimum force required to prevent it from sliding down is $F_2$. If $\theta > \tan^{-1}\mu_s$, then $(F_1 - F_2)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
1. Force to pull up: $F_1 = mg\sin\theta + \mu_s mg\cos\theta$.
2. Force to prevent slipping down: $F_2 = mg\sin\theta - \mu_s mg\cos\theta$.
3. Difference: $F_1 - F_2 = 2\mu_s mg\cos\theta$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m$ slides down an inclined plane of inclination $\theta$ with variable friction coefficient given by $\mu(x) = kx$, where $x$ is the distance travelled from the top rest position. The maximum distance $x_{\text{max}}$ travelled by the block before it stops is:
questions.solution:
Integrating work done from $x = 0$ to $x = x_{\text{max}}$:
$$\int_0^{x_{\text{max}}} (mg\sin\theta - kx mg\cos\theta)\,dx = 0 \implies x_{\text{max}}\sin\theta - \frac{1}{2}k x_{\text{max}}^2\cos\theta = 0 \implies x_{\text{max}} = \frac{2\tan\theta}{k}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In Question 6, the position $x$ where the block achieves its maximum velocity is:
questions.solution:
Velocity is maximum when acceleration is zero: $mg\sin\theta - \mu(x)mg\cos\theta = 0 \implies kx\cos\theta = \sin\theta \implies x = \frac{\tan\theta}{k}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m = 5\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough inclined plane of inclination $\theta = 30^\circ$ ($\mu_s = 0.7$). The magnitude of the frictional force acting on the block is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
Angle of repose is $\phi = \tan^{-1}(0.7) \approx 35^\circ$. Since $\theta = 30^\circ < \phi$, the block does not slide.
Self-adjusting static friction balances the downhill component of gravity: $f_s = mg\sin 30^\circ = 5 \times 10 \times 0.5 = 25.0\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m$ is pushed up a rough inclined plane of inclination $\theta$ by a horizontal force $F$. The normal reaction $N$ exerted by the incline on the block is:
questions.solution:
Resolving forces perpendicular to the incline: $N = mg\cos\theta + F\sin\theta$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In Question 9, the minimum horizontal force $F$ required to just move the block of mass $m$ up the rough inclined plane ($\mu_s$) is:
questions.solution:
Balancing forces along the plane at impending upward motion:
$$F\cos\theta = mg\sin\theta + \mu_s(mg\cos\theta + F\sin\theta)$$
$$F(\cos\theta - \mu_s\sin\theta) = mg(\sin\theta + \mu_s\cos\theta) \implies F = mg\left[\frac{\sin\theta + \mu_s\cos\theta}{\cos\theta - \mu_s\sin\theta}\right]$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A block is placed on a rough inclined plane whose inclination $\theta$ can be varied. The time taken by the block to slide down a fixed length $L$ of the plane is minimum when the angle of inclination $	heta$ satisfies:
questions.solution:
For a fixed vertical height $h$ ($L = h/\sin\theta$), time $t = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g\sin\theta(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta)}}$. Minimizing $t$ yields the optimal angle $\theta = 45^\circ + \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\mu_k$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A body of mass $m$ is released from height $h$ from rest on a rough inclined plane of angle $	heta$ and base length $b$. The work done by friction as the body reaches the bottom of the incline is:
questions.solution:
$$W_f = -f_k \cdot L = -(\mu_k mg\cos\theta)\left(\frac{b}{\cos\theta}\right) = -\mu_k mg b$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Two blocks of masses $m_1 = 2\text{ kg}$ and $m_2 = 4\text{ kg}$ connected by an inextensible light string slide down an inclined plane of angle $\theta = 37^\circ$. If the coefficient of friction for $m_1$ (upper block) is $\mu_1 = 0.4$ and for $m_2$ (lower block) is $\mu_2 = 0.2$, the tension in the string during downward motion is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Common acceleration: $a = \frac{(m_1 + m_2)g\sin 37^\circ - (\mu_1 m_1 + \mu_2 m_2)g\cos 37^\circ}{m_1 + m_2} = \frac{36 - 12.8}{6} = 3.867\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. For $m_1$: $m_1 g\sin 37^\circ - \mu_1 m_1 g\cos 37^\circ + T = m_1 a \implies 12 - 6.4 + T = 2(3.867) \implies T = 2.13\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In Question 13, if the positions of the two blocks are reversed so that $m_2$ ($\mu_2 = 0.2$) is above $m_1$ ($\mu_1 = 0.4$), the tension in the connecting string becomes:
questions.solution:
When the upper block has lower friction than the lower block, it accelerates faster down the slope than the lower block, causing the string to become slack ($T = 0\text{ N}$).
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A block is released from rest at the top of a rough incline ($\mu_k = 0.25, \theta = 45^\circ$). If the length of the incline is $16\text{ m}$, the time taken by the block to slide down is ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Acceleration: $a = 9.8\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \frac{0.25}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 5.197\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. Time taken: $t = \sqrt{\frac{2L}{a}} = \sqrt{\frac{32}{5.197}} \approx 2.48\text{ s}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m$ slides down a rough curved ramp of height $h$ and arrives at the bottom with speed $v = \sqrt{gh}$. The work done by friction along the curve is:
questions.solution:
By Work-Energy Theorem: $W_g + W_f = \Delta K \implies mgh + W_f = \frac{1}{2}m(gh) \implies W_f = -\frac{1}{2}mgh$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A triangular wedge of mass $M$ and inclination $	heta$ rests on a smooth horizontal floor. A block of mass $m$ is placed on its rough face ($\mu$). The maximum horizontal acceleration $a$ of the wedge to the right so that the block does not slide up the incline is:
questions.solution:
In wedge frame: $N = mg\cos\theta + ma\sin\theta$. Impending upward slide: $ma\cos\theta = mg\sin\theta + \mu N \implies a = g\left[\frac{\sin\theta + \mu\cos\theta}{\cos\theta - \mu\sin\theta}\right] = g\tan(\theta + \lambda)$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A block is projected up an incline with speed $u$. After reaching the highest point, it slides down. If the ratio of kinetic energy at return to initial kinetic energy is $\eta$ ($\eta < 1$), the coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu_k$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\eta = \frac{K_f}{K_i} = \frac{\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta}{\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta} = \frac{\tan\theta - \mu_k}{\tan\theta + \mu_k} \implies \mu_k = \tan\theta\left(\frac{1 - \eta}{1 + \eta}\right)$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$ is kept on an inclined plane of inclination $\theta = 45^\circ$ ($\mu_s = 0.8$). A force $F$ is applied horizontally to keep the block in equilibrium. The range of $F$ for static equilibrium is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. $F_{\text{min}} = mg\left[\frac{\sin 45^\circ - 0.8\cos 45^\circ}{\cos 45^\circ + 0.8\sin 45^\circ}\right] = 10\left(\frac{0.2}{1.8}\right) = \frac{10}{9} \approx 1.11\text{ N}$.
2. $F_{\text{max}} = mg\left[\frac{\sin 45^\circ + 0.8\cos 45^\circ}{\cos 45^\circ - 0.8\sin 45^\circ}\right] = 10\left(\frac{1.8}{0.2}\right) = 90\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A wooden block of mass $m$ resting on an incline $	heta$ is connected to a hanging mass $M$ via a light string passing over a frictionless pulley at the top. The minimum mass $M$ required to just prevent the block $m$ from sliding down the incline ($\mu_s < \tan\theta$) is:
questions.solution:
At impending downward motion, static friction acts uphill: $T + f_s^{\text{max}} = mg\sin\theta \implies Mg + \mu_s mg\cos\theta = mg\sin\theta \implies M_{\text{min}} = m(\sin\theta - \mu_s\cos\theta)$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.
